security_audit.summary: All 400 presented static findings are false positives involving illustration code, assets, dependency metadata, or expected local tooling. One additional finding identifies unescaped scene labels that can inject HTML into contact sheets; no evidence found of keylogging, credential theft, or audit manipulation. The analyzer capped review at 400 of 2,018 matches; the remaining 1,618 are unconfirmed and require manual review before automatic publishing. Static review was capped at 400/2018 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 1618 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Scene labels are inserted as HTML into generated contact sheets.
remediation.suggestion: In scripts/film.mjs, render captions with textContent or HTML escaping, and test labels containing markup. Disable scripting and external requests when rendering sheets.

remediation.issue: The static analysis cap leaves 1,618 matches unconfirmed.
remediation.suggestion: Complete manual adjudication of the omitted matches before automatic publishing. Keep the distinction between reviewed findings and unconfirmed matches visible.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped Scene Labels Can Alter Capture Evidence
semantic_findings.description: State capture reads page-controlled data-mark values and inserts them unescaped into contact-sheet HTML. Crafted labels can inject styles or scripts, falsifying review images or initiating browser requests.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source directly connects data-mark attributes to shot labels and interpolates those labels into setContent without escaping. Exploitation requires control of a captured label; no malicious payload was observed.

content.user_title: Create Product UI Illustrations and Animated Demos
content.value_statement: Product illustrations can look unfinished when layout, typography, and motion lack consistent structure. Stageshow provides React components, reference scenes, and capture tools for realistic product visuals.
actual_capabilities: Compose product scenes with reusable browser windows, phones, notifications, terminals, and interface controls.
Script simulated cursor movement, typing, clicks, scrolling, and dragging through the Act API.
Animate changing values, expanding panels, connected objects, and streaming text with dedicated motion components.
Define wide and compact scene layouts, playback behavior, and poster states for reduced motion.
Capture PNG stills and contact sheets with Playwright and an installed Chrome or Chromium browser.
Check scene geometry, layout fit, motion discontinuities, and CSS namespace collisions with included scripts.
limitations: Scenes illustrate interfaces; simulated clicks do not automate real applications or provide production business logic.
Integration requires React, react-dom, lucide-react, and the relevant CSS; capture tools also require Node.js, Playwright, and Chrome or Chromium.
Automated checks do not replace visual review, responsive layout work, or assessment of complete animation loops.
Contact-sheet labels need escaping, and the capped security review leaves additional static matches awaiting manual adjudication.

use_cases.title: Design Product Launch Visuals
use_cases.description: Create a focused product illustration with authentic interface structure, deliberate cropping, and a clear result.

use_cases.title: Embed Feature Walkthroughs
use_cases.description: Integrate a scripted cursor demo into an existing React page with compact layouts and a meaningful poster state.

use_cases.title: Illustrate Documentation Workflows
use_cases.description: Show one interface task through a short sequence, then capture stills or contact sheets for documentation review.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Still Illustration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Stageshow to create a still illustration of [product screen] for a [width] by [height] space. Start from the closest reference scene.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create one focused product image.

prompt_templates.title: Animate One Interface Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Stageshow demo showing [task] in three to five beats. Use measured cursor targets, a visible result, and a meaningful reduced-motion poster.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt an Existing Product
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the closest Stageshow scene to [product] using our typography, colors, and components. Provide separate wide and compact layouts without shrinking interface text.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: integrate a scene into a branded React page.

prompt_templates.title: Rehearse and Verify a Demo
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [demo] at desktop and mobile widths using Stageshow capture tools on a trusted local preview. Inspect motion, report defects, and document unchecked states.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: validate visual quality before handoff.

output_examples.input: Create a still illustration of a customer dashboard for a feature section.
output: A cropped dashboard window with one selected customer, restrained supporting rows, and a visible total.
A compact composition that preserves readable labels and the same focal result.

output_examples.input: Show a form error being corrected in an animated demo.
output: A cursor enters a field, an error appears beside that field, and corrected text clears the error.
The submit button confirms success, while the poster shows the completed state.

output_examples.input: Review a demo for mobile layout and animation defects.
output: Desktop and mobile contact sheets with observations about cropping, text fit, cursor placement, and motion continuity.
A handoff note listing inspected states, remaining defects, and checks that were not completed.

best_practices: Start from the closest reference scene and preserve its structure before replacing the product look and content.
Design compact layouts explicitly, measure cursor targets, and choose a poster that shows the result.
Capture only trusted previews, inspect complete loops visually, and treat automated checks as supporting evidence.
anti_patterns: Treating simulated interactions as real browser automation or a production application.
Shrinking an entire desktop scene into a mobile column instead of composing a compact layout.
Approving a demo from one still image or an automated pass without reviewing its full motion.

faq.question: What does Stageshow create?
faq.answer: It creates authored product UI illustrations and scripted walkthroughs using React components and plain CSS.

faq.question: Does it control real applications?
faq.answer: No. The Act API draws interactions and changes scene state rather than operating a real product.

faq.question: Which dependencies are required?
faq.answer: The kit uses React, react-dom, and lucide-react. Capture scripts require Node.js, playwright-core, and an installed Chrome or Chromium browser.

faq.question: Can I use my existing components?
faq.answer: Yes. Place your components inside a Stage and map your product styles to the scene instead of using every supplied part.

faq.question: How are mobile and reduced-motion views handled?
faq.answer: Define a compact layout for narrow spaces and a poster state that communicates the result when motion is reduced.

faq.question: Is the security review complete?
faq.answer: The 400 presented alerts were adjudicated, but 1,618 capped matches remain unconfirmed. Unescaped contact-sheet labels also require remediation.
